gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Shure's MV7+ manual says XLR audio is not affected by software settings, so Auto Level, the denoiser and the other MOTIV features drop out once the mic goes into an interface. The results also don't give the makers' XLR sensitivities, which show the Samson Q9U (−57 dBV/Pa) needs about 6 dB more preamp gain than the Maono PD400X (−51 dBV) and 2 dB more than the MV7+ (−55 dBV/Pa).
standout_why: I could read only one result in full, itechguides.com. It says the AmpliGame AM8's controls and headphone monitoring turn off over XLR, and that on the MV7+, PodMic USB and NT1 'USB and XLR remain different signal paths'. It never says the MV7+ or PodMic USB processing stops on XLR, and it gives no XLR sensitivity for any of the hybrid mics (its only figure is the SM7B's −59 dBV/Pa). Both cited MusicRadar pages loaded as a title plus a truncation notice, so I could not check them. A cited rival may cover part of this, which is why the score is 2 and not 3.
decides: This confirms the MV7+ as the pick for a USB-only buyer. It also adds a warning: ChatGPT's reason for picking it (auto gain and denoising) disappears when the shopper 'upgrades to an audio interface', because Shure says software settings don't affect XLR audio. Over XLR, the PD400X's hotter −51 dBV output suits a low-gain interface better than the Q9U's −57 dBV/Pa. The Q9U also shows 'Coming Soon' and unavailable on Samson's own page today, so it is a weak budget pick to send people to.

findings.label: Effect of software DSP on the XLR output
findings.value: "Note: XLR audio is not affected by software settings." (user guide p. 6)
findings.source_title: Shure MV7Plus manual (reproduction of Shure's MV7+ user guide)
findings.note: Shure's own guide at https://www.shure.com/en-US/docs/guide/MV7+ loaded only its navigation, so this quote comes from the ManualsLib copy. The software settings are the MOTIV Mix DSP: Auto Level, Real-time Denoiser, Digital Popper Stopper and presets.

findings.label: XLR sensitivity
findings.value: −55 dBV/Pa (1.78 mV) at 1 kHz, open-circuit voltage, XLR connection
findings.note: The USB-C figure on the same page is −33 dBV/Pa. The page lists the labels and values separately, so I matched them by order.

findings.label: App and OS compatibility
findings.value: MOTIV Mix desktop: Windows 10 or later and macOS 12 or later, with at least 8 GB RAM and 20% free disk space; MOTIV Audio & Video apps: iOS 16 or later and Android 12 or later

findings.label: Where the APHEX DSP applies
findings.value: On-board APHEX DSP is described for the digital USB output only
findings.note: The page says the mic has 'powerful on-board DSP (Digital Signal Processing) powered by APHEX®' and ties it to the USB connection. It says nothing about DSP on the XLR output.

findings.label: Device compatibility
findings.value: Windows and Mac computers, iOS and Android devices; RØDE Central needs macOS 11 or later, or Windows 10 version 1803 or later
findings.note: Also works with RØDE Connect, RØDE Capture and UNIFY. An external pop filter is in the box.

findings.label: XLR and USB sensitivity
findings.value: XLR −57 dBV/Pa (1 kHz); USB −16 dBFS/Pa (0 dB gain, 1 kHz)
findings.note: That is 2 dB lower than the MV7+ (−55) and 6 dB lower than the Maono PD400X (−51), so it needs that much more interface gain over XLR.
